issue.title: [asyncpg] Extract rowcount for SELECT statements
issue.body:
### Description
Postgres does return a rowcount for `SELECT` statements.
https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/protocol-message-formats.html#PROTOCOL-MESSAGE-FORMATS-COMMANDCOMPLETE

Closes: #9048

body:
I would be -1 on this (no pun intended) if this only works on asyncpg.    ~~DBAPI rowcount is only supposed to be for DML statements~~ we generally discourage the use of "rowcount" for plain SELECT statements as there is very little driver support for this and it also has major performance implications as it implies the database needs to retrieve the entire result set, and maybe even sending it to the client.

If this is relevant to a CTE INSERT, then it should work for all the PostgreSQL drivers and we'd need all-pg-backend tests which exercise this.  the bug would be that no test is exercising this right now.

> If this is relevant to a CTE INSERT, then it should work for all the PostgreSQL drivers and we'd need all-pg-backend tests which exercise this. the bug would be that no test is exercising this right now.

It does work for psycopg2 at least, I can check the other drivers.

All the other postgresql drivers support it already (I haven't tested py-postgresql because I think it needs an older python version). #9049 adds a test for this (is `MiscBackendTest` the right place?)
miscbackend is probably fine sure.    psycopg2, psycopg, and asyncpg are the three we normally try to keep together

**Michael Gorven** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **main** branch:

**[asyncpg] Extract rowcount for SELECT statements** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/4340

**Michael Gorven** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **rel_1_4** branch:

**[asyncpg] Extract rowcount for SELECT statements** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/4343

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

All releases after 2.0.0rc2 appear to have the behavior described, while the releases i tested before it (2.0.0rc1, all the betas, 1.4.X, 1.3X) work fine.

```
sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError: (pymysql.err.OperationalError) (1049, "Unknown database 'fooschema'")
[SQL: DESCRIBE `fooschema`.`foo`]
```
You'll see the reproduction code below but essentially `event.listen(metadata, "before_create", CreateSchema("fooschema"))` appears to fail to execute the `before_create` event.

Replacing that line with `conn.execute(CreateSchema("fooschema"))` works just fine.

### To Reproduce

```python
docker run -d -e MYSQL_DATABASE=database -e MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=password -p 3306:3306 -it mysql:8
```

```python
from sqlalchemy import engine, MetaData, event, types, Column
from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.schema import CreateSchema

metadata = MetaData()
Base = declarative_base(metadata=metadata)


class Foo(Base):
    __tablename__ = "foo"
    __table_args__ = {"schema": "fooschema"}

    id = Column(types.Integer(), primary_key=True)


engine = engine.create_engine("mysql+pymysql://root:password@localhost:3306/database")
with engine.connect() as conn:
    event.listen(metadata, "before_create", CreateSchema("fooschema"))
    metadata.create_all(conn)
```
